content_metadata.description: An instructional video showing how to fix a common HP printer issue: the carriage jam, with a mix of critique of HP's design choices.

qAndA.answer: The waste tank sucker is positioned too high, causing it to lock with the carriage.
qAndA.question: What is the primary reason for the carriage jam in this printer?
Which direction do you need to turn the gear to lower the platform?

qAndA.answer: It's the position where the sucker is all the way out and the printhead platform is raised to conceal the printhead.
qAndA.question: What is the 'cap position' of the waste tank sucker?

qAndA.answer: He believes they intentionally made the mechanism complex and prone to failure, potentially to encourage users to buy new printers.
qAndA.question: Why does the technician criticize HP's design?

qAndA.answer: They can contact him locally in Greensboro, North Carolina.
qAndA.question: Besides visiting the website, how else can viewers get help from the technician?

youtube_description:
Does your print carriage stuck on the right of the printer (service station)? Learn how to fix a carriage jam in your HP OfficeJet and clear the error: Carriage Jam: The print carriage cannot move.  Open the cartridge access door, clear any paper jam or obstruction, and select "OK". Watch this video then.

Part Two:
If you have a broken PFG gear at 0:36 (the gear I circled out), check this out: https://bchtechnologies.com/search.php?search_query=pfg&section=product
Replace PFG in HP OfficeJet Pro 90xx (9018): https://youtu.be/wY1QD4VEtLg

Hewlett Packard troubleshooting
HP Officejet Pro 
HP paper jam
